related_questions.question: What does zoonotic do to humans?
related_questions.snippet: Zoonotic diseases are caused by harmful germs like viruses, bacterial, parasites, and fungi. These germs can cause many different types of illnesses in people and animals, ranging from mild to serious illness and even death.

text_blocks.snippet: To prevent zoonotic diseases, focus on good hygiene, safe food handling, and protecting yourself from animal bites and scratches. This includes frequent handwashing, especially after contact with animals, avoiding contact with bodily fluids, and taking precautions when visiting animal exhibits or handling animals. Vaccinating pets, controlling vectors like mosquitos and ticks, and practicing safe food preparation are also crucial.
snippet_highlighted_words: focus on good hygiene, safe food handling, and protecting yourself from animal bites and scratches

list.title: Wash hands frequently:
list.snippet: Wash your hands thoroughly with soap and water, especially after being around animals, before eating, and after handling animal waste.

list.title: Use hand sanitizer:
list.snippet: If soap and water are not available, use an alcohol-based hand sanitizer with at least 60% alcohol.

list.title: Avoid touching your face:
list.snippet: Avoid touching your eyes, nose, and mouth, especially before washing your hands.

list.title: Avoid contact with sick or wild animals:
list.snippet: Be cautious around animals that appear unwell and avoid contact with stray or wild animals.

list.title: Prevent bites and scratches:
list.snippet: Be mindful of your interactions with animals, and take precautions to avoid bites or scratches.

list.title: Protect wounds:
list.snippet: Keep any cuts or wounds covered, especially when handling animals.

list.title: Use personal protective equipment (PPE):
list.snippet: Wear gloves and other appropriate protective clothing when handling animals, cleaning animal areas, or dealing with animal waste.

list.title: Supervise children:
list.snippet: Ensure children wash their hands after playing with pets or visiting animal areas.

list.title: Cook meat thoroughly:
list.snippet: Cook all meat, especially pork and poultry, to a safe internal temperature to kill foodborne zoonotic agents.

list.title: Avoid unpasteurized dairy:
list.snippet: Do not consume unpasteurized milk or dairy products.

list.title: Wash fruits and vegetables:
list.snippet: Wash fruits and vegetables thoroughly, especially if they will be eaten raw.

list.title: Separate raw and cooked food:
list.snippet: Prevent cross-contamination by keeping raw and cooked foods separate during preparation.

list.title: Control mosquitoes, ticks, and fleas:
list.snippet: Use insect repellent, wear protective clothing, and take measures to reduce mosquito and tick populations around your home.

list.title: Keep pets vaccinated and protected from parasites:
list.snippet: Consult with your veterinarian about vaccinations and parasite control for your pets.
Clean animal areas: Regularly clean and disinfect areas where animals live, including cages, litter boxes, and feeding areas.
Dispose of waste properly: Dispose of animal waste in a sanitary manner.
Avoid contact with contaminated water: Avoid drinking from or swimming in potentially contaminated water sources.

list.title: Consult a doctor:
list.snippet: If you experience symptoms of a zoonotic illness, seek medical advice promptly.

list.title: Be aware of zoonotic risks:
list.snippet: Be aware of the potential risks associated with different animals and environments, especially when traveling or visiting public animal exhibits.

text_blocks.snippet: By taking these precautions, you can significantly reduce your risk of contracting a zoonotic disease.

text_blocks.snippet: Zoonotic diseases, those transmissible from animals to humans, can manifest with a wide array of symptoms. These can range from general, flu-like symptoms like fever, fatigue, and body aches, to more specific signs like skin lesions, gastrointestinal issues (diarrhea, vomiting), or even neurological symptoms in severe cases. The specific symptoms experienced depend heavily on the particular disease and its severity.
snippet_highlighted_words: general, flu-like symptoms like fever, fatigue, and body aches, to more specific signs like skin lesions, gastrointestinal issues (diarrhea, vomiting), or even neurological symptoms in severe cases

text_blocks.snippet: Here's a more detailed look at potential symptoms:

list.snippet: Fever, chills, and body aches: These are common early signs of many zoonotic infections.
Fatigue and weakness: Zoonotic diseases can cause significant tiredness and a general feeling of being unwell.
Headache: Headaches are another frequently reported symptom.
Swollen lymph nodes: Inflamed lymph nodes, particularly near the site of infection, can be a sign.
Skin lesions, rashes, or sores: Some zoonotic diseases can cause visible skin changes.
Diarrhea: Often watery and sometimes bloody.
Nausea and vomiting: These can occur alongside or independently of diarrhea.
Abdominal pain or cramps: Can range from mild discomfort to severe cramping.
Loss of appetite: A decreased desire to eat is a common symptom.
Cough: Can be dry or productive.
Shortness of breath: May indicate a more serious respiratory infection.
Chest pain: Less common but can occur in severe cases.
Confusion and disorientation: Can be a sign of neurological involvement.
Hallucinations and seizures: Rare but possible in severe cases.
Hydrophobia (fear of water): A characteristic symptom of advanced rabies.
Rabies: Characterized by neurological symptoms, including hydrophobia and paralysis.
Cat Scratch Disease: May cause swollen lymph nodes near the bite or scratch, fever, and fatigue.
Salmonella: Often causes gastrointestinal symptoms like diarrhea, vomiting, and abdominal pain.
Avian Influenza: Can cause flu-like symptoms, eye inflammation, or severe respiratory illness.
Cryptosporidiosis: Causes severe diarrhea, abdominal cramps, and nausea.
Hookworm: Causes itchy, raised tracks on the skin where the parasite burrows.

text_blocks.snippet: If you experience any unexplained symptoms, particularly if you've had contact with animals or suspect a zoonotic disease, it's crucial to consult a medical professional for prompt diagnosis and treatment.
